title: Idle Surface Mapping - weekly brief and experiment log
summary: Weekly standing note capturing the idle surface mapping experiment, micro-burst hedging readouts, kernel preselect telemetry, and action items for regional capacity optimization.
notes:
Context and hypotheses:
- Problem: high churn in small request workloads causes a lot of short GPU prewarm/warmup cycles in certain regions (eu-west-2, us-central-1). We observe waste because GPUs are being provisioned for short bursts and then sitting idle while still billed to reserved pools.
- Hypothesis: by constructing an "idle surface map" (heatmap of where idle capacity actually exists and how quickly it can accept specific model families), the scheduler can reduce unnecessary prewarming and instead route short bursts to nearby pools with compatible kernel/quantization profiles. This should lower transient cost and reduce tail latency caused by repeated prewarm jitter.

This week's objectives:
1) Validate idle-surface mapping with a small Canary across eu-west-2 and us-central-1.
2) Collect kernel preselection telemetry (which kernels selected within first 30s of instance life) and assess compatibility collisions for two model families (redwood-13b-quant, mosaic-vicuna-7b-fp16).
3) Run micro-burst hedging (20–90s bursts) against hedged pools and measure cost delta and P95/P99 latency.

What we ran:
- Canary window: 2029-10-09 02:00 -> 2029-10-10 02:00 (24h)
- Traffic shape: sampled replay of PROD small-chat workload at 3x baseline for 10-minute islands, separated by 15 minute gaps to force short-life allocations.
- Routing change: lightweight scheduler flag enabled idle-surface scoring (score = proximity*compatibility*(1 - cold_penalty)).
- Kernel telemetry: instrumented runtime to emit initial kernel choices and sequence of kernel swaps during first 120s. Data pushed to /logs/idle-surface-canary-20291009 in S3.

Observations (TL;DR):
- Idle surface improved short-burst absorption: temporary routing to hedged pools increased from 19% -> 54% of short-burst allocations in canary zones.
- Cost: estimated token-billed GPU-hour equivalent for the canary dropped by ~11% vs baseline (mainly from fewer cold starts).
- Latency: P95 tail for small-chat in the canary decreased 7%, P99 decreased 4%. Median unchanged.
- Kernel collisions: ~9% of rerouted requests needed a kernel swap because target pool lacked the precise quantized kernel; 87% of those completed kernel swap within 180ms and did not impact end-to-end tail significantly.
- Failure modes: one hedged pool (eu-west-2-b) hit memory fragmentation causing OOM throttles for large embeddings jobs; correlated with a background model-rollover job from team-models.

Detailed metrics (summary numbers from canary):
- Short-burst allocations (<= 90s): baseline absorption by hedged pools 19% -> 54% with idle-surface (absolute uplift +35%).
- Cold-start incidence (requests that saw cold inference jitter): 0.22 -> 0.09 per 1k requests.
- Estimated transient GPU-hour saved (canary window scaled): 1.8 GPU-hours saved / 24h.
- Cost delta (probe estimate normalized to $/GPU-hour): -11% transient cost for this workload shape.
- Kernel swap rate on reroutes: 9% (of rerouted requests) with median swap latency 92ms, 95th swap latency 210ms.

Root causes / notes:
- Memory fragmentation in eu-west-2-b lineage is a known issue (ticket INFRA-7631). The hedged pool policy currently does not factor in recent fragmentation events; need to add a fragmentation penalty.
- Kernel compatibility matrix is incomplete for mosaic-vicuna-7b-fp16 on some older instance types (g7x-legacy); team applied a hotpatch to install missing kernels during the canary which increased swap latency.
- Scheduler scoring hyperparameters (proximity weight, compatibility binary vs graded compatibility) matter; current default overweights proximity which caused some suboptimal hedges (higher kernel swap rate).

Decisions and proposals:
1) Add a fragmentation factor to hedged pool scoring (weight 0.4) and re-run canary on 2029-10-16. Owner: Diego Alvarez, due 2029-10-15. Jira: INFRA-7892.
2) Expand kernel compatibility matrix ingestion: add nightly reconcile job that compares installed kernel set vs desired matrix per model family. Owner: Marissa Chen, PR: runtime#4421, due 2029-10-14.
3) Tune scoring: reduce proximity weight by 20% and move compatibility to graded score (0..1) rather than binary. Run AB for 48h to confirm swap rate <6%. Owner: Liam O'Connor, due 2029-10-17.
4) Emergency safeguard: if hedged pool swap latency >400ms for 5m window, revert to baseline routing for that pool and alert SRE. Implement circuit breaker. Owner: Priya Shah + SRE rotation, RFC in next standup, due 2029-10-13.

Open action items (short list):
- INFRA-7892: add fragmentation factor to hedged scoring (Diego) – blocked by access to fragmentation telemetry (SRE infra ticket).
- runtime#4421: kernel matrix reconciler (Marissa) – review requested.
- AB test config change (Liam) – set up AB channels and traffic split (33/33/34).
- Postmortem for eu-west-2-b OOM event (SRE) – initial notes in linked_artifacts.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: aggressive hedging could push more small-burst traffic into a smaller set of physical hosts causing local noisy-neighbor effects. Mitigation: add per-pool absorb-rate cap (default 12% of pool capacity) and test.
- Risk: kernel swap overhead on certain instance types increases end-to-end latency. Mitigation: prioritize installing commonly used kernels in high-absorb hedged pools and ship reconciler job as high priority.

Next steps for next weekly update (proposed):
- 2029-10-16: hedged scoring run across three regions (eu-west-2, us-central-1, ap-southeast-1) with fragmentation factor enabled.
- Add a synthetic micro-burst benchmark (open-sourced harness) to be run as part of CI every weekend to detect regressions in hedged absorption. Owner: Diego + Eng QA.
- Dashboard: add idle-surface map visualization widget to Console (early prototype in /dash/idle-surface-canary) to help SREs inspect which pools were chosen and why. Owner: Product Console team (linked ticket: CONSOLE-582).

Meeting notes (10/10 sync, attendees):
- Priya Shah (chair), Liam O'Connor, Marissa Chen, Diego Alvarez, SRE pager on-call (Anika Patel), Product Console (Jae Kim)
- Quick wins agreed: nightly kernel reconciler, fragmentation penalty, circuit breaker.
- Longer discussion: whether to expose a per-customer hint API for preferred hedging (customers with strict latency can opt-out). Agreed to prototype an annotation in the config API (product to spec).

Attachments and artifacts locations:
- Canary logs: s3://redwood-infra/idle-surface-canary-20291009/
- Kernel telemetry aggregated: s3://redwood-infra/idle-surface-canary-20291009/kernel-telemetry-agg.csv
- JIRA: INFRA-7834 (canary tracker), INFRA-7892 (fragmentation), INFRA-7631 (eu-west-2-b fragmentation)
conclusion: Early signal is positive: idle-surface mapping meaningfully increases short-burst absorption and reduces transient cost and tail latency for the tested workload. Key next steps are addressing kernel compatibility and memory fragmentation signals before broad rollout.
